searches.note: Twenty five searches of a share of twenty eight, none of them the author's. Eight were restricted to a house's or a body's own domain (blandy.com with madeirawinecompany.com and bhsportugal.org, blandys.com, henriquesehenriques.pt with its importers twice, vinhosbarbeito.com twice, hmborges.com, and dica.madeira.gov.pt with vinhomadeira.com and the house twice) and are read as primary through their summaries where the domain is the house's or the body's; four more kept the house's own domain out so that the second source would be independent (Blandy's and the Madeira Wine Company, Henriques & Henriques, Barbeito, H.M. Borges). The three shared searches are the island's serving guidance (DICA and the H.M. Borges FAQ), the wine institute's rules for estufagem and canteiro, and the swap ruling (the owners of Justino's and Henriques & Henriques). No WebFetch was tried. Three searches were left unspent.

method: Each record was read with one instruction, refute it: the founding year, the people and their dates, the classification, the grapes, the sites, the making and its months, the drinking window, the serving temperature, the label words, every beat of the story, the cards and the questions; then the house rules (nobody living named, no price, no score, nothing volatile, no judging superlative, no bare family word, British spelling, no dash).

The searches went first to the open web, with the house's own domain kept out, for the second source of each date and person, then to the houses' own pages for their own dates, sites and methods, then to the regional government (DICA) and the wine institute (vinhomadeira.com) for the serve and the rules.

Where a search contradicted the record it was set right with its source; where a detail was found in no source of this check and in one of the author's only, it was cut or said with less (the convent's suppression of 1835, the move to cooler floors, the export slump of 1913, the Blandys' controlling share of the late 1970s, the thirty exporters of 1946, the skins of the H.M. Borges fermentation, blue cheese).

Facts of a house's own history told on its own pages stand, hedged as the house's account where the story tells them so; a person is named only with dates from the house's page or two sources (John Blandy, Mário Barbeito de Vasconcelos), and every other founder or heir stays described.

Sources whose title or address names a living writer, or a writer's own site, were met among the results but are cited neither in the fragment nor here; the fragment's sources were left as the author wrote them except where one is replaced, and the new ones are listed per record under extraSources.

tested: John Blandy (1783 to 1855): 1783 is on the Blandy group's own history page (primary for its founder), and 1855 on that page and in an outside account; the arrival of 1808 with a letter of introduction dated December 1807 is in the Arquivo Histórico da Madeira, the Madeira Wine Company and the British Historical Society of Portugal, which also report the tradition of a soldier of Beresford's garrison of 1807; the record's 1808 stands.

1811 with two of his brothers, a wine shipper and general trader, trade to Russia, northern Europe, the West Indies and North America: the Blandy group's page names the brothers Thomas and George and gives the markets (the Antilles for the West Indies); the Arquivo Histórico da Madeira has him set up on the Rua de São Francisco as a wine exporter in 1811. Confirmed.

The lodge and the convent: the regional government's culture page has the São Francisco buildings as largely all that remains of the Franciscan convent, and a travel guide puts the lodge on the convent's grounds; beside it was wrong, and 1835 for the suppression was in no source read. Changed.

1913, 1925, 1981: company histories (FundingUniverse, Encyclopedia.com and others) give the Association of 1913 formed by export houses to pool costs, Blandy's and Leacock's joining in 1925, and the name Madeira Wine Company in 1981; the slump and the Blandys' controlling share by the late 1970s were in none (control after 1974 is given to the Blandy and Leacock families together). Changed.

1989 and 2011: the Symington partnership of 1989 and the Blandys' regaining of control in 2011 are in the Madeira Wine Company's pages as the author read them and in two outside accounts, one of which says the Symingtons took a majority in 1989, which the record's into partnership does not deny. Confirmed.

The making: the house's 10 Year Old sheets give natural yeasts at 18 to 21 degrees Celsius in steel, fortification with grape spirit at 96 per cent early in fermentation, canteiro in seasoned oak and an average age of ten years; the move downward through the lodge's floors was in neither sheet, and the wine institute has canteiro casks in the warm upper floors only. Changed.
The serve: the house's newer 10 Year Old sheet gives 16 degrees Celsius, slightly chilled after dinner; its Malmsey page says no higher than 15. About 16 stands, with the difference left open.
The trap on estufagem: the wine institute gives 45 to 50 degrees Celsius for no less than three months. Changed for precision.

The questions: one key each; the wine question's options are four ways of ageing and the story question's four Port families; the explanation of the first now says the younger blends without a judgement. Sound after the change.

The rules: nobody living named (the 1989 partners are a family, named as a firm of Port shippers); no price, no score; sweetest is the ladder of the four noble grapes, which the library and the island's rules give; British; no dash. Sound.

tested: 1850, the founder's death in 1912, the two sons' partnership and the name, the company of 1913, exports from 1925, the cellar and the Quinta Grande centre of 1992: Mentzendorff, the Madeira Wine Guide and other merchants agree on each, one giving the sons as Francisco Eduardo and João Joaquim and one the consolidation into a company in 1913. Confirmed.

The founder of an old landowning family of Câmara de Lobos: the accounts read have him found the firm as a partidista supplying other shippers from the family's extensive vineyards; the house is widely described as the one Madeira house to have owned vineyards without a break. Confirmed in substance; he stays described, since no birth year was found.

Quinta Grande between 350 and 700 metres, planted mostly with Verdelho, and the 15 Year Old Verdelho from it: the house's vineyards page and its importer give 350 to 700 metres, and the importer has the 15 Year Old from Quinta Grande, in canteiro for at least fifteen years. Confirmed, and the sites line is rightly hedged.

Oidium in 1852 and phylloxera in 1872: outside histories give oidium's arrival in 1851 and the early 1850s, and the regional government the middle of the century; phylloxera in 1872 in most, 1871 or 1872 in the Elucidário Madeirense. Oidium changed to the early 1850s.
The Terrantez of the others line, medium dry: the house's Terrantez 20 years page and its importer both give medium dry. Confirmed.
The serve, 13 to 16 degrees Celsius, the older the warmer: DICA gives 13 to 14 for younger Madeira and 15 to 16 for older. Confirmed.
The questions: one key each, four steps of the ladder and four years; the explanations teach the ladder and 1913. Sound.

The rules: the founder and sons described; the house's winemaker met in a summary is not named; no price, no score; largest is the house's own largest vineyard, in the house's and its importer's pages; British; no dash. Sound.

tested: Mário Barbeito de Vasconcelos (1905 to 1985), born in Funchal: the house's Avô Mário page gives both years and Funchal (primary for its founder); the Rare Wine Co and the house give 1985 and his daughter's taking charge. Confirmed.

A collector of books on the island's history and on Columbus: the house's page has his library of more than twenty five thousand volumes on Madeira, Columbus and the discovery of America, and Funchal's museum library in his name holds a Columbus collection. Confirmed.

1946 and a hard time to begin: the house, the Rare Wine Co and a wine blog agree on 1946; the importer and a merchant have him enter the trade in a hard period for Madeira. The thirty exporters and the sales fallen low through the war were in no source of this check. Changed.
The Kinoshita family from 1967 and the joint venture of 1991: Cellar Tours and Decantalo give 1991, and the house's own history, quoted by a merchant, 1967 and 1991. Confirmed.
The grandson in charge in the early 1990s: one account gives 1993, the house 1989 for his joining; early 1990s stands.
No caramel: Lea & Sandeman, a merchant and a wine writer's review agree that the grandson stopped adding caramel. Confirmed; the author's doubt is settled.
First to name Tinta Negra on a label: one outside article on the house's press page says so; hedged as the house's account, it stands.
The Malvasia 20 Years Old from São Jorge, in numbered lots: Uncorked and other merchants give São Jorge and the lot numbers (Lote 21333 among them). Confirmed.
O Japonês: merchants and the importer give a limited fifty year old Malvasia dedicated to the house's Japanese partner, who died in 2003. Confirmed, and now called a limited bottling.
The questions: one key each, four meanings of a number and four partners; the explanations teach the lot and the Symingtons' partnership with Blandy's. Sound.
The rules: the founder named with dates; the daughter, the grandson and the Japanese partner described; no price, no score; British; no dash. Sound.

swaps.proposed: The author set out, for the checker, a possible swap of H.M. Borges for Cossart Gordon or for Justino's, while keeping H.M. Borges.
swaps.why: Cossart Gordon is a brand of the Madeira Wine Company, which the group already holds through Blandy's, and the plan never takes two producers of one house. Justino's and Henriques & Henriques are both controlled by the same French group by outside accounts, so Justino's would put two picks of one owner in the group. H.M. Borges is an independent family house of 1877 with a full canteiro range, sound on its sources, and stays.
